# `tier3_suppliers`

> **GENERATED** — rendered from the data contract. Edit [`supabase/contract/tier3_suppliers.contract.yaml`](../../../supabase/contract/tier3_suppliers.contract.yaml)

**Tier 2** — canonical — the only tier humans edit · owned by `data-ingestion` · `public.tier3_suppliers`

**One row is** One tier-3 supply relationship: a tier-2 supplier and the supplier BEHIND it, for one material. The row is an EDGE, not a party; the schema is the same as `tier2_suppliers` because the fact is the same fact one hop further out.

DESCRIBED IN PHASE 3 / WP 3.2, having been deferred under WP 3.1's group since WP 1.4. The deferral said these were "the other inbound datasets, each with its own bespoke upload path", and this package is the one that gives them the shared one: a tier3_suppliers CSV is now parsed server-side, landed in tier 0, staged in `ingest_staged_rows` and promoted by `ingest_apply_run` like any other lane. WHAT IS STILL TRUE AND UNCOMFORTABLE: the table has no natural-key constraint (D5's shape, WP 3.3) and no audit trigger (WP 2.3 instrumented twelve tables and could not instrument one the contract did not describe). Both are recorded above rather than rounded off, because a sidecar that describes the table it wishes existed is worth less than none.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `tier3_suppliers_pkey` |
| `project_id` + `plant_name` + `supplier_id` + `upstream_supplier_id` + `material_id` | UNIQUE index | `tier3_suppliers_natural_key` |

**Natural key:** `project_id` + `plant_name` + `supplier_id` + `upstream_supplier_id` + `material_id` — the key this table's grain implies, and the
database ENFORCES it: `tier3_suppliers_natural_key`. A re-upload of the same row updates
it rather than duplicating it.

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `editor` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 2 — all carry a predicate |

Two policies, both routed through the project's organization — `org_is_current_user_org(p.organization_id, p.organization)` for SELECT and the same predicate plus modeler-or-admin for writes. It is the dual-read shape WP 3.0 made uuid-only at the predicate (D29); the one remaining text branch is `organizations`' own read policy (D47, WP 6.2), not this one. `audited: true` SINCE WP 3.2, and the sequence is worth keeping. WP 2.3 instrumented twelve tier-2/3/4 tables and this was not among them, because nothing in the contract described it: `dataPlaneAudit.test.ts` requires the three triggers on every tier-2/3/4 table IN THE CONTRACT, so a table with no sidecar was outside the rule and nobody could see that its writes were unattributable. Writing this sidecar turned that gate red in the same session, and `20260916000016` is the gate being obeyed rather than a decision taken. It matters here more than most: `ingest_apply_run` promotes a CSV into this table, and a promotion into an unaudited table is the `audit-actor` hole this package exists to close.

| Tier3: organization access view | SELECT | all | `20260915000004_org_identity_dual_read.sql` |
| Tier3: project access modify | ALL | all | `20260915000004_org_identity_dual_read.sql` |

</details>
